title: Microsoft Places: workplace app for hybrid work comes to GCC High
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap targets, feature switches, administrator paths and licensing statements are supported. It distinguishes general Places documentation from unpublished GCC High details and reports the conflicting group-scoping guidance rather than promising that it works.

claims.claim: Microsoft's organisation-wide turn-off procedure disables core feature settings and then Places Enhanced for all users.
claims.quote: To turn off Microsoft Places for everyone in your organization, you'll need to turn off Places Core features using tenant settings, then disable the Places Enhanced service plan for all users in your organization.

claims.claim: At the time of writing the four feature switches are documented through PowerShell, with no alternative admin-centre or Graph setting operation found.

claims.claim: The documented Places licensing model is mixed, combining included core features, per-space premium features and Copilot-licensed AI features.

claims.claim: The medium cost rating reflects additional licences for selected premium capabilities rather than only indirect administration time.

claims.claim: EnableBuildings has an effect only after buildings and floors have been configured.

claims.claim: At most 20 OIDs can be used when limiting feature access.
claims.quote: A maximum of 20 OIDs can be used when limiting feature access.

claims.claim: Unlike the reference's OID restriction, the analytics page documents a group-scoped SpaceAnalyticsEnabled example.
claims.quote: For example, to enable analytics for users in a specific mail-enabled security group: Set-PlacesSettings –SpaceAnalyticsEnabled 'Default:false,OID:507121fd-a361-40a1-907b-2ca512e6ce50@1a2a08524-022b7-4bab7-8a8c-bc2c4006201c:true'

claims.claim: Buildings are enabled for analytics separately from granting user access.
